per_event_streaming_first_pass.why_wrong: over-counts when P is non-monotone: mid-tick transients that revert to P>=1.6 by the end-of-tick boundary do not page a real tick monitor. The 5.5 caught this.

mitigation_note: a 'persist N ticks' confirmation window is NOT adopted: it would be a new rule chosen AFTER seeing the fires (exploratory at best), it can only DELAY a page that already arrives after most of the data is gone, and it would not suppress the 849-tick non-transient page.
takeaway: Offline headline numbers (H7 0 false pages, 7/7) are whole-run properties. Causally (tick-boundary, triple-verified): (a) H7 catches the swarm but after a median ~61% exfiltration at the 300-s tick -- fails high at every phase; (b) H7 has a small honest false-page rate (2 of 5 fresh seeds, phase-robust) the whole-run scoring hides, and one honest page is non-transient (~2.95 days). Both are honest limitations; neither overturns the thesis (the swarm is caught; prevention needs friction, not a faster pager).
